name: Apache Airflow (self-hosted)
sku: Apache Airflow 3.3 run on hosts that you operate: the scheduler, web server, workers and metadata database are yours, on its local or Celery executors. Its code-first design is central, so it suits teams that prefer workflows as Python code to a graphical designer. The engine is the same on every host, so the Kubernetes, Astronomer and managed records repeat its scores; managed hosts are Amazon MWAA, Cloud Composer and Data Factory in Fabric.

orchestrate.dependency-dag.note: A Dag encapsulates everything needed to run a workflow: its schedule, tasks, dependencies and callbacks. Workflows are defined entirely in Python, and a wide range of built-in operators and providers connect tasks to other systems.

orchestrate.scheduling.note: Rich scheduling semantics for complex recurring pipelines, with manual triggering, backfilling of historical data and targeted task reruns.

bands.note: A web-based UI to visualise, manage and debug workflows across deployment scales. It shows workflow runs; it does not check the data the tasks produce.

The OpenLineage provider has shipped in Airflow itself since 2.7, automatically emitting lineage events (DAG, task and run metadata, plus dataset input/output where an operator supports it) on every run. It is the emitter, not the graph: a backend such as Marquez or a catalog that consumes OpenLineage events is needed to see the result.

presentation.tagline: Open-source workflows as Python code: schedule, run and monitor data pipelines.
